title: Enough points from a cover by finitary slices
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] in the fixed universe convention [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $(U_i)_{i\in I}$ be a set-indexed family of objects such that the coproduct of the associated sheaves of their representable presheaves $\coprod_{i\in I}h_{U_i}\to 1$ is an epimorphism in $\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$. Here $h_U$ denotes the sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] of $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(-,U)$, without any subcanonicity assumption. Assume that for every $i$, the slice site $\mathcal C/U_i$ with its localized topology [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] has finite limits and every covering family in it admits a finite covering refinement. Then $\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$ has a set-indexed family of points $p_j:\mathbf{Set}\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$ whose inverse-image functors jointly reflect isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 00YN, lemma-criterion-points: a cover of the final object by objects whose slices satisfy Proposition 00YQ

proof.text: The covering axioms [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] pass to C/U_i. Induction on Precoverage.Saturate, using bind composition rather than arbitrary repeated indexed composition, shows that a covering sieve contains an actual covering presieve. Pulling such presieves to the slice identifies the generated slice topology with J.over U_i [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Transport the slice to AsSmall, with both object and morphism universe max u v [def-weil-size-convention]. Lift covering arrows and finite refinements through AsSmall.up/down; the transported presieve site satisfies the same three axioms. Apply [lem-trf-finitary-site-enough-points] there, and transport its points and conservativity back through Mathlib Equivalence.sheafCongr. The private Lean lemmas asSmall_site, asSmall_dense, exists_cover, over_site, over_topology and finitarySite_large_enoughPoints prove all this glue completely.

For each U_i, Mathlib supplies continuity and cocontinuity of Over.forget, its sheafAdjunctionCocontinuous, and preservation of finite limits by its continuous sheaf restriction. These construct the localization geometric morphism directly, with inverse image J.overPullback. Compose this morphism with each slice point using [def-trf-geometric-morphism]. No separate covering-level topos-adjunction theorem or special-cocontinuity predicate is needed.

Write P for the presheaf coproduct of the lifted representables and T for the constant singleton presheaf. Sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] preserves coproducts and terminal objects. The composite of its coproduct comparison, the sheafification of P to T, and the terminal isomorphism is the assumed epimorphism; hence the sheafification of P to T is epic. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-epi-locally-surjective] it is locally surjective. Use the already proved general unit_locally_surjective helper from the module of [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local], which requires only HasWeakSheafify and no stronger precoverage composition class. The unit at T is an isomorphism. Naturality of the unit therefore gives local surjectivity of P to T. On every object the image sieve of the singleton section is covering. A local section of P belongs to some representable summand, so its domain maps to U_i for some i. Enlarging the image sieve to Sieve.ofObjects U proves J.CoversTop U. The private coversTop_of_epi proves this for arbitrary value universe max u v w.

Index the composite points by the dependent sum of the slice index types, in the same fixed universe [def-weil-size-convention]. If every composite inverse image takes a sheaf map a to a bijection, slice conservativity makes every J.overPullback(a) invertible. Apply the proved Mathlib lemma Sheaf.isIso_of_coversTop to the cover of Step 3 and these restriction isomorphisms. This yields IsIso a, including when the family is empty.

split_report.summary: Split the finite-cover slice criterion into four steps. For each slice, apply the existing finite-cover enough-points theorem and transport its points through the localized-site/sheaf-slice equivalence; then use the assumed epimorphic coproduct of representables to descend local isomorphisms to the whole sheaf topos. No new nodes were needed because all non-elementary inputs already exist in the DAG.
split_report.blueprint: The steps realize the auxiliary enough-points criterion used by the current module-factorization route; the imported blueprint contains no separate enough-points paragraph, so the proof follows Stacks Tag 00YN explicitly.

tool_uses.why: Steps 1-2 apply Deligne's finite-cover criterion (Stacks 00YQ) to each slice as a black box; it is a general site-theoretic theorem filed in sec-trace-formula and no node of this unit states it.
Step 1 takes from it that restriction along the continuous cocontinuous forgetful functor C/U->C is the inverse image of a morphism of topoi; generic site lemma of sk-thm-properbasechange.
Step 3 uses that sections of a sheafification are locally sections of the presheaf; generic sheafification lemma of sk-thm-p1.
Step 3 uses that epimorphisms of sheaves of sets are locally surjective (Mathlib leaf).
